PokeDaisy is a Game Boy, Game Boy Color, Game Boy Advance and Nintendo DS player for Android, made for Pokémon games. Beside your game runs a live

that reads it while you play: your party, your bag, the map you're on, how the current battle is going, your Pokédex and a guide that hints before it tells. On a dual-screen handheld like the AYN Thor, the companion gets the bottom screen to itself. On a handheld with one screen it opens as a window over the game or a panel beside it, and on a phone held upright it sits under it.
You never have to pause and open a menu to check a Pokémon's moves or look up what an attack does against a type. One glance, and it's there, drawn in the game's own menu style.

Losing a 40-hour save is the worst thing an emulator can do, so PokeDaisy is careful with it:
A backup every time you start a game.
Before the game opens its save, PokeDaisy copies it into a

Resuming never overwrites a newer save.

A save in progress always finishes.

Hardcore would have to switch off things PokeDaisy is built around: loading save states (including picking up where you left off when you open a game), rewind, and the companion's battle buttons, which press the game's buttons for you.

blocks.text: My game didn't resume where I left it

c.text: When a game opens, PokeDaisy normally puts you back exactly where you were. Before it does, it checks that your save file hasn't changed since that point. If it has (you played the same save in RetroArch, moved your saves folder, or copied a save in), resuming would put the old save back over the newer one. So PokeDaisy sets the old resume point aside and starts the game from your save file instead. Your newest save wins.
